items.title: Gateway Process Assessment
items.summary: A 1983 report by Army Lt. Col. Wayne McDonnell assessing the Monroe Institute's Gateway Experience, a course of audio tapes meant to synchronize the brain's hemispheres (Hemi-Sync). It tries to explain the course's claims of out-of-body states and perception beyond time and space in terms of physics, drawing on Itzhak Bentov's models.
items.credit: U.S. Army (Lt. Col. Wayne M. McDonnell, US Army Operational Group, Fort Meade)

facts.claim: Dated 9 June 1983 and signed by Lt. Col. Wayne M. McDonnell of the US Army Operational Group, Fort George G. Meade, as an assessment of the Gateway Experience.
Stamped 'Approved For Release 2003/09/10' under CREST number CIA-RDP96-00788R001700210016-5.
Describes the Monroe Institute's Hemi-Sync technique, induced with audio tapes, and relies on Itzhak Bentov's biomedical models to explain out-of-body states.

items.title: Mars Exploration, May 22, 1984
items.summary: Transcript of a May 1984 remote-viewing session in which the viewer held a sealed envelope, opened only afterwards, with a card reading 'The planet Mars. Time of interest approximately 1 million years B.C.' Given a series of coordinates, he describes pyramids and very tall, thin 'ancient people' who are dying.
items.credit: U.S. Army remote viewing program (Stargate records released by the CIA)

facts.claim: Titled 'Mars Exploration, May 22, 1984'; the sealed envelope, not opened until after the session, held a 3x5 card reading 'The planet Mars. Time of interest approximately 1 million years B.C.'
The viewer reports a pyramid form and 'very tall... thin' people, later saying 'They're ancient people... they're dying'.
Stamped 'Approved For Release 2000/08/08' under CREST number CIA-RDP96-00788R001900760001-9.
The viewer, Joseph McMoneagle, said the Mars session was requested by an individual from the Army, not the CIA.

items.title: Pat Price's Crane Drawing
items.summary: A page from Kenneth Kress's 1977 CIA article comparing a crane at a Soviet research site near Semipalatinsk (URDF-3) with the crane that remote viewer Pat Price drew at SRI in July 1974, after being given the site's coordinates and told it was a Soviet test site. Analysts agreed the crane was accurate, but most of Price's other data were wrong or could not be checked.
items.credit: Central Intelligence Agency (Studies in Intelligence, Winter 1977); sketch by Pat Price
items.license: US government work (CIA), public domain; the sketch was made by an SRI test subject for a CIA-funded experiment

facts.claim: Figure 1, 'Comparison of Target Site and Drawing by Remote Viewer', shows the URDF-3 target site and a crane comparison; Price was given the geographic coordinates, an atlas map marked with the site and the fact that it was a Soviet test site, and produced the drawing overnight.
The URDF-3 experiment started on 9 July 1974 at SRI, with the target 60 miles WSW of Semipalatinsk.
Analysts agreed Price's crane was accurate, but 'most of Price's data were wrong or could not be evaluated'.
The page is stamped 'Approved For Release 2003/04/18'.

items.title: Experiments: Uri Geller at SRI
items.summary: Stanford Research Institute notes, from the CIA's files on its SRI contract, on eight days of tests in August 1973 in which Uri Geller tried to copy drawings he could not see, either locked in a shielded room or while the targets were drawn on the East Coast. The researchers wrote that he had shown paranormal perception 'in a convincing and unambiguous manner'.
items.credit: Stanford Research Institute, for the Central Intelligence Agency
items.license: Declassified CIA record, no known copyright restrictions (contractor report by SRI)

facts.claim: Headed 'EXPERIMENTS - Uri Geller at SRI, August 4-11, 1973'; Geller was separated from targets by an electrically isolated shielded room or by having targets drawn on the East Coast.
The report says Geller 'demonstrated his paranormal perceptual ability in a convincing and unambiguous manner'.
Stamped 'Approved For Release 2003/03/28' under CREST number CIA-RDP79-00999A000300030027-0.

items.title: Parapsychology in Intelligence
items.summary: CIA officer Kenneth Kress's account of the agency's psychic research, written for its classified journal Studies in Intelligence in 1977. It covers the SRI work, Pat Price's viewing of a Soviet test site and Price naming Kress's CIA job, and argues the results were never properly assessed.

facts.claim: Published in Studies in Intelligence, Vol. 21 No. 4, Winter 1977, as 'Parapsychology in Intelligence: A Personal Review and Conclusions' by Dr. Kenneth A. Kress.
Kress writes that Price, asked his occupation, answered 'Works for CIA' while Kress was a covert employee.
Kress concludes that 'sufficient understanding and assessment of parapsychology has not been achieved' and that some observations 'defy explanation'.
Stamped 'Approved For Release 2003/04/18'.

items.title: Psychics and the Dozier Kidnapping
items.summary: Slides from a 1983 Army briefing on its remote viewers' sessions to locate Brigadier General James Dozier, kidnapped by the Red Brigades in Verona in December 1981. The slide for 20 January 1982 reads 'The name is Padua'; Italian police, helped by a US Army intelligence unit, freed Dozier from a Padua apartment on 28 January 1982.
items.credit: U.S. Army Intelligence and Security Command (Center Lane project)

facts.claim: Catalogued as '1983 Briefing Papers - Use of Center Lane Relocation of BG Dozier in Italy'.
The viewgraph for 20 Jan 82 reads 'Data on city: The name is Padua'; the 26 Jan 82 entry says the subject is handcuffed to a metal pipe or rail.

Dozier was kidnapped from his Verona apartment in December 1981 and held for 42 days until 28 January 1982, when Italian police, helped by the Army's Intelligence Support Activity, rescued him from an apartment in Padua.
Stamped 'Approved For Release 2000/08/08'.

items.title: Coordinate Remote Viewing (1985)
items.summary: A secret February 1985 working paper on Coordinate Remote Viewing, the training method developed by Ingo Swann with SRI, in which a viewer tries to describe a site given only its geographic coordinates. It sets out the six training stages and includes a sample session.
items.credit: U.S. Army remote viewing program (Center Lane)

facts.claim: Titled 'Coordinate Remote Viewing, Stages I-VI and Beyond, February 1985' and marked as a SECRET working paper.
Defines CRV as 'the process by which a person is capable of perceiving information concerning a site remote from him in location and/or time given only the geographic coordinates'.
Describes the method as developed by I. Swann, building on research at SRI International.
Stamped 'Approved For Release 2000/08/07'.

items.title: An Evaluation of Remote Viewing
items.summary: The 1995 review of the government's remote-viewing program by the American Institutes for Research, commissioned by the CIA, with assessments by statistician Jessica Utts and psychologist Ray Hyman. It found remote viewing had never been used to guide intelligence operations and concluded that continued use was not warranted; the program was closed that year.
items.credit: American Institutes for Research (Michael D. Mumford, Andrew M. Rose, David A. Goslin), for the Central Intelligence Agency
items.license: Declassified CIA record, no known copyright restrictions (contractor report by AIR)

facts.claim: 'An Evaluation of Remote Viewing: Research and Applications' by Mumford, Rose and Goslin of the American Institutes for Research is dated September 29, 1995.
The review panel included Dr. Jessica Utts (statistics, UC Davis) and Dr. Raymond Hyman (psychology, University of Oregon).
It concluded that 'continued use of remote viewing in intelligence gathering operations is not warranted' and that the information was never used to guide operations.
The CIA commissioned the report and the program was terminated and declassified in 1995.

rejected.title: Experiments with Uri Geller (SRI film, 1973)
rejected.reason: Filmed by Stanford Research Institute, not a government body, and the copy on archive.org/Commons was spliced by MuckRock and The Black Vault from copies of mixed origin; I found no official CIA or NARA release of the film, so it fails the release and copyright rules despite its PD-USGov tag on Commons.

rejected.title: Gateway Process exhibits (Commons PNGs, e.g. Exhibit 5 'cosmic egg')
rejected.reason: Striking diagrams, but the report credits its exhibits to Itzhak Bentov's 1977 book Stalking the Wild Pendulum (Exhibit 1 is labelled as taken from it), so they are probably copyrighted reproductions.

rejected.title: An Analysis of a Remote-Viewing Experiment of URDF-3 (CIA, 1975)
rejected.reason: Verified and downloadable (CIA-RDP96-00791R000200240001-0, 34 pages, released 2001-03-07), and it holds Price's original crane sketches and an analyst's verdict that the experiment was unsuccessful, but the Kress article and the crane figure already cover the same experiment. Good substitute if more items are wanted.

rejected.title: Iranian Hostage Situation, Summary Analyses (Grill Flame)
rejected.reason: The CREST item (CIA-RDP96-00788R001000330003-3) is only a 2-page cover sheet with no session content.

rejected.title: DIA Psychoenergetics Activity, Action Memo to the Deputy Secretary of Defense (1985)
rejected.reason: Interesting Pentagon approval memo, but only 2 pages, and its release-date stamp is illegible, so the released date could not be confirmed; less interesting than the Dozier briefing.

rejected.title: Hal Puthoff photo (Commons, from CIA-RDP96-00788R001200300004-3)
rejected.reason: A plain portrait of low interest, and the photo's authorship (likely SRI or a press photo) is unclear, so the PD-USGov tag is doubtful.

rejected.title: Coordinate Remote Viewing Manual (Paul H. Smith, 1 May 1986)
rejected.reason: The widely shared copy was posted publicly by Smith in 1998 and was never given an official release; used the CREST-released February 1985 'Stages I-VI and Beyond' paper instead.

rejected.title: Video or audio of Stargate sessions
rejected.reason: None found from a government source: CREST holds only transcripts and drawings, and the TV coverage (e.g. ABC Nightline, 1995) is copyrighted. This topic's non-document item is the crane drawing image.
